adrs.title: Parallelism model: file-disjoint slices + Jev lane decisions
adrs.decision: Shared-file contention was the only thing serialising module slices, so: (1) src/app.js auto-mounts every src/routes/*.js at /<basename> (alias map for /administration) — slices never edit app.js; (2) src/db.js applies db/migrations/*.sql in filename order inside the schema transaction — each slice owns one idempotent file. Module slices are therefore code-independent; remaining dependencies in the registry are DATA dependencies only (S7 needs S6 scores, S8 needs S2+S5 data, S10 needs S2 records). Lane choice is a Jev decision via codemode (one call, atomic questions); all five current slices scored parallel_safe 0.85 and needs_heavy_lane < 0.6 -> flash-fleet x5 concurrently.
evidence: all 11 routes verified 200 after the refactor

adrs.title: Jev lane decisions + schema-supplied dispatch for data-coupled slices
adrs.decision: Wave 2 slices are DATA-coupled (S7 posts from grading tables, S8 reports over student/attendance data, S4 builds the rosters S5 approximates) though still file-disjoint. Jev scored parallel_safe only 0.51-0.69 and flagged needs_heavy_lane for S4 (0.75) and S7 (0.73). Response: keep parallelism (reads only, no cross-slice writes), route the two hard slices to glm-swarm, and supply each worker the verified schema of every table it may read so it cannot invent columns. Lesson recorded: when parallel_safe drops, look for data coupling and answer it with schema contracts, not serialisation.
evidence: four dispatches with read-only schema blocks

adrs.title: Free-lane concurrency limit (OpenRouter shared pool)
adrs.decision: OpenRouter ':free' models work but draw on a SHARED upstream pool and return 429 under parallel load: two of six wave-3 agents died within 15s with 0 tokens while the same models answered fine when tested serially. Rule for free lanes: at most 2 concurrent per free model, and never more than 3 free-lane agents in one wave; route the remainder to flash-fleet. Zen's space-bunny-free did not show this (separate provider) but is likewise unproven at high concurrency. Free lanes remain ideal for serial work — sweeps, single-file verification, first-pass reviews.
evidence: serial sweep of the same models passed
